newsitem.title: NEPAL: Earthquakes rock Nepal, but no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Earthquakes rock Nepal, but no casualties.

text.p: Nepal's Kathmandu valley was rocked by two earthquakes and several tremors early on Saturday but there were no reports of casualties, officials said.
The tremors woke many residents during Friday night and created a minor panic in the mountainous capital of the Himalayan kingdom.
Officials said a first tremor at 11 p.m. (1715 GMT) was followed by a second, stronger earthquake measuring 5.8 on the open-ended Richter scale at 1.47 a.m. (2002 GMT).
"So far we have not received any reports of casualties," a Home (interior) Ministry spokesman said.
The officials said the epicentre was in Rasuwa district, northeast of Kathmandu. They said at least three aftershocks with intensities between 4.3 and 4.7 were felt in the capital.
"We felt the tremor when we were fast asleep," Kathmandu resident Sunil Sharma said. "I rushed to call my parents who were sleeping on the upper floor and we ran out of the house."
Officials at the National Seismological Centre described the first earthquake as a "pre-shock" measuring 5.0 on the Richter scale and described the later shock as the main earthquake.
"It was not a large earthquake but a medium-sized one," Ramlochan Prasad Tandukar, the chief geologist at the centre, told Reuters.
Residents of Rasuwa said by telephone they felt tremors until late morning on Saturday.
"Houses have developed cracks and some could collapse if further tremors are felt," a police official said.
Earthquakes between five and six on the Richter scale are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in populated areas.
More than 700 people were killed when an earthquake measuring 6.5 on the Richter scale hit Udayapur in eastern Nepal in 1988.
